claim: Telomeric G-quadruplexes were long believed to form a protective structure at telomeres, preventing their extension by the ribonucleoprotein telomerase.
source: Telomeric G-quadruplexes (G4) were long believed to form a protective structure at telomeres, preventing their extension by the ribonucleoprotein telomerase.
evidence: This is a statement about prior scientific belief, supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Parallel-stranded conformations of telomeric G4 can be extended by human and ciliate telomerase.
source: Contrary to this belief, we have previously demonstrated that parallel-stranded conformations of telomeric G4 can be extended by human and ciliate telomerase.
evidence: This claim is supported by previous work from the authors, as indicated by the phrase 'we have previously demonstrated'.

claim: Binding is initiated by the RNA template of telomerase interacting with the G-quadruplex.
source: Binding is initiated by the RNA template of telomerase interacting with the G-quadruplex; nucleotide addition then proceeds to the end of the RNA template.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from smFRET and enzymatic assays presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nucleotide addition proceeds to the end of the RNA template.
source: Binding is initiated by the RNA template of telomerase interacting with the G-quadruplex; nucleotide addition then proceeds to the end of the RNA template.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with subsets of dNTPs showing extension to the template boundary.

claim: The G-quadruplex structure is completely unfolded through the large conformational change of translocation following synthesis.
source: It is only through the large conformational change of translocation following synthesis that the G-quadruplex structure is completely unfolded to a linear product.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data showing a second FRET drop after nucleotide addition reaches the template boundary.

claim: Parallel G4 stabilization with small molecule ligands does not always inhibit G4 unfolding and extension by telomerase.
source: Surprisingly, parallel G4 stabilization with either small molecule ligands or by chemical modification does not always inhibit G4 unfolding and extension by telomerase.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with NMM, SST16, and PhenDC3 showing that telomerase can still unfold and extend stabilized G4 structures.

claim: Parallel G4 stabilization by chemical modification does not always inhibit G4 unfolding and extension by telomerase.
source: Surprisingly, parallel G4 stabilization with either small molecule ligands or by chemical modification does not always inhibit G4 unfolding and extension by telomerase.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with 2'F-araG modified oligonucleotides showing telomerase extension despite increased thermal stability.

claim: Telomerase is a parallel G-quadruplex resolvase.
source: These data reveal that telomerase is a parallel G-quadruplex resolvase.
evidence: This conclusion is drawn from the collective experimental data showing telomerase's ability to unfold and extend parallel G4 structures.

claim: Human chromosomes contain many guanine (G)-rich elements capable of forming four-stranded G-quadruplex (G4) structures.
source: Human chromosomes contain many guanine (G)-rich elements capable of forming four-stranded G-quadruplex (G4) structures (Bochman et al., 2012; Huppert and Balasubramanian, 2005; Maizels and Gray, 2013; Rhodes and Lipps, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: A planar G-quartet is formed when four Gs form hydrogen bonds in a cyclical manner via their Hoogsteen faces.
source: A planar G-quartet is formed when four Gs form hydrogen bonds in a cyclical manner via their Hoogsteen faces; such G-quartets stack on top of each other and form G-quadruplexes (Sen and Gilbert, 1988; Sundquist and Klug, 1989; Williamson et al., 1989).
evidence: This is established knowledge about G-quadruplex structure, supported by citations.

claim: G-quartets stack on top of each other and form G-quadruplexes.
source: A planar G-quartet is formed when four Gs form hydrogen bonds in a cyclical manner via their Hoogsteen faces; such G-quartets stack on top of each other and form G-quadruplexes (Sen and Gilbert, 1988; Sundquist and Klug, 1989; Williamson et al., 1989).
evidence: This is established knowledge about G-quadruplex structure, supported by citations.

claim: G-rich sequences are primarily located in promoter regions, intron and exon boundaries, origins of replication and telomeres.
source: G-rich sequences are primarily located in promoter regions, intron and exon boundaries, origins of replication and telomeres (Bochman et al., 2012; Huppert and Balasubramanian, 2005; Maizels and Gray, 2013; Rhodes and Lipps, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Vertebrate telomeres consist of many tandem repeats of the sequence TTAGGG, comprising a double-stranded region and a 3' G-rich overhang.
source: Vertebrate telomeres consist of many tandem repeats of the sequence TTAGGG, comprising a double-stranded region and a 3' G-rich overhang (Blackburn, 1991).
evidence: This is established knowledge about telomere structure, supported by a citation.

claim: Fluorescence microscopy studies have shown the existence of G4 structures at the telomeric regions of fixed human cells using G4-specific antibodies.
source: Fluorescence microscopy studies have shown the existence of G4 structures at the telomeric regions of fixed human cells using G4-specific antibodies (Biffi et al., 2013; Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: In vitro, telomeric DNA can adopt many different conformations of G4, including inter- or intramolecular forms, arranged in parallel or anti-parallel orientation depending upon the directionality of the DNA backbone.
source: In vitro, telomeric DNA can adopt many different conformations of G4, including inter- or intramolecular forms, arranged in parallel or anti-parallel orientation depending upon the directionality of the DNA backbone (Burge et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Conditions that may mimic those in the nucleus, including high DNA concentration and water depletion, favour parallel conformations of human telomeric G4.
source: Conditions that may mimic those in the nucleus, including high DNA concentration and water depletion, favour parallel conformations of human telomeric G4 (Heddi and Phan, 2011; Miller et al., 2010; Renciuk et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: The in vivo conformation(s) and biological significance of telomeric G4 in human cells remain elusive and undetermined.
source: However, the in vivo conformation(s) and biological significance of telomeric G4 in human cells remain elusive and undetermined.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Telomere shortening occurs with every cell division in normal human somatic cells, since conventional DNA polymerases cannot completely synthesize the telomeric end.
source: Telomere shortening occurs with every cell division in normal human somatic cells, since conventional DNA polymerases cannot completely synthesize the telomeric end (Harley et al., 1990; Olovnikov, 1971; Watson, 1972).
evidence: This is established knowledge about telomere biology, supported by citations.

claim: Telomerase extends telomeric DNA in cancer cells, stem cells and cells of the germline, using a unique mechanism of processive rounds of reverse transcription.
source: Telomerase, a telomere-specific ribonucleoprotein enzyme complex, extends telomeric DNA in cancer cells, stem cells and cells of the germline, using a unique mechanism of processive rounds of reverse transcription (Greider and Blackburn, 1985; Hiyama and Hiyama, 2007; Kim et al., 1994; Morin, 1989; Podlevsky and Chen, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about telomerase function, supported by citations.

claim: Human telomerase minimally consists of the highly conserved telomerase reverse transcriptase protein (hTERT) and an RNA component containing an 11 nucleotide (nt) template sequence (hTR).
source: Human telomerase minimally consists of the highly conserved telomerase reverse transcriptase protein (hTERT) and an RNA component containing an 11 nucleotide (nt) template sequence (hTR) (Wyatt et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge about telomerase composition, supported by a citation.

claim: Telomerase extends its telomeric substrate by first binding to telomeric DNA, followed by hybridization of the RNA template with the DNA.
source: Telomerase extends its telomeric substrate by first binding to telomeric DNA, followed by hybridization of the RNA template with the DNA.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the telomerase mechanism.

claim: Telomerase extends the substrate DNA by using its RNA as a template for nucleotide addition to the DNA 3' end.
source: Second, telomerase extends the substrate DNA by using its RNA as a template for nucleotide addition to the DNA 3' end.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the telomerase mechanism.

claim: Once the template 5' boundary has been reached, telomerase translocates downstream, resulting in re-alignment of the RNA template with the new 3' end of the product DNA.
source: Once the template 5' boundary has been reached, telomerase translocates downstream, resulting in re-alignment of the RNA template with the new 3' end of the product DNA (Greider and Blackburn, 1989; Podlevsky and Chen, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the telomerase mechanism, supported by citations.

claim: One function of telomeric G4 may be to act as a 'cap', protecting the telomere from DNA degradation.
source: One function of telomeric G4 may be to act as a 'cap', protecting the telomere from DNA degradation (Smith et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: It has been widely believed that G4 formation within the 3' telomeric overhang blocks telomere extension by telomerase.
source: It has been widely believed that G4 formation within the 3' telomeric overhang blocks telomere extension by telomerase, since early in vitro studies had shown that G4 structures inhibit telomerase extension of a telomeric DNA substrate (Zahler et al., 1991; Zaug et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a statement about prior scientific belief, supported by citations.

claim: Early in vitro studies had shown that G4 structures inhibit telomerase extension of a telomeric DNA substrate.
source: It has been widely believed that G4 formation within the 3' telomeric overhang blocks telomere extension by telomerase, since early in vitro studies had shown that G4 structures inhibit telomerase extension of a telomeric DNA substrate (Zahler et al., 1991; Zaug et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Stabilization of G4 with small-molecule ligands has been shown to more effectively inhibit telomerase activity.
source: In addition, stabilization of G4 with small-molecule ligands has been shown to more effectively inhibit telomerase activity, suggesting that chemical stabilization of G4 structures may be a viable anti-cancer therapeutic strategy (De Cian et al., 2007a; Gomez et al., 2016; Sun et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Chemical stabilization of G4 structures may be a viable anti-cancer therapeutic strategy.
source: In addition, stabilization of G4 with small-molecule ligands has been shown to more effectively inhibit telomerase activity, suggesting that chemical stabilization of G4 structures may be a viable anti-cancer therapeutic strategy (De Cian et al., 2007a; Gomez et al., 2016; Sun et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on prior experimental work, as indicated by 'suggesting'.

claim: The above-mentioned studies did not distinguish between G4 conformations, and used oligonucleotides that likely folded into anti-parallel or 'hybrid' G4 forms as a telomerase substrate.
source: However, the above-mentioned studies did not distinguish between G4 conformations, and used oligonucleotides that likely folded into anti-parallel or 'hybrid' G4 forms as a telomerase substrate.
evidence: This is an inference based on analysis of prior studies.

claim: A variety of helicases, such as RECQ5, WRN, BLM, FANC-J and RHAU, recognize and resolve G4 in a conformation-specific manner.
source: A variety of helicases, such as RECQ5, WRN, BLM, FANC-J and RHAU, recognize and resolve G4 in a conformation-specific manner (Budhathoki et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2010; London et al., 2008; Tippana et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Telomerase can bind and extend specific conformations of telomeric G4 - those that are parallel-stranded and intermolecular.
source: Similarly, we have demonstrated that telomerase can bind and extend specific conformations of telomeric G4 - those that are parallel-stranded and intermolecular - and that this property of telomerase is well conserved from ciliates to human (Moye et al., 2015; Oganesian et al., 2007; Oganesian et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work from the authors.

claim: The property of telomerase to bind and extend parallel-stranded and intermolecular G4 is well conserved from ciliates to human.
source: Similarly, we have demonstrated that telomerase can bind and extend specific conformations of telomeric G4 - those that are parallel-stranded and intermolecular - and that this property of telomerase is well conserved from ciliates to human (Moye et al., 2015; Oganesian et al., 2007; Oganesian et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work from the authors.

claim: If telomeric G-quadruplexes were to adopt a parallel conformation in vivo, they may indeed be extended by telomerase.
source: This suggests that if telomeric G-quadruplexes were to adopt a parallel conformation in vivo, they may indeed be extended by telomerase, contrary to what had been previously hypothesized.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the authors' prior experimental work.

claim: Telomerase extension reactions in the presence of individual nucleotides demonstrated that the 3' end of a G4 substrate aligns correctly with the RNA template of telomerase.
source: Telomerase extension reactions in the presence of individual nucleotides demonstrated that the 3' end of a G4 substrate aligns correctly with the RNA template of telomerase, suggesting that at least partial resolution of G4 structure is required for telomerase extension (Moye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work from the authors.

claim: At least partial resolution of G4 structure is required for telomerase extension.
source: Telomerase extension reactions in the presence of individual nucleotides demonstrated that the 3' end of a G4 substrate aligns correctly with the RNA template of telomerase, suggesting that at least partial resolution of G4 structure is required for telomerase extension (Moye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference based on prior experimental work, as indicated by 'suggesting'.

claim: The evidence for partial disruption of the G4 was indirect.
source: However, the evidence for partial disruption of the G4 was indirect, and a mechanistic understanding of telomerase resolution of G4 DNA, in the absence of a known helicase function of hTERT, remained elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of prior work.

claim: A mechanistic understanding of telomerase resolution of G4 DNA, in the absence of a known helicase function of hTERT, remained elusive.
source: However, the evidence for partial disruption of the G4 was indirect, and a mechanistic understanding of telomerase resolution of G4 DNA, in the absence of a known helicase function of hTERT, remained elusive.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: All previously-tested substrates were both parallel-stranded and intermolecular.
source: Furthermore, since all previously-tested substrates were both parallel-stranded and intermolecular, it was unknown which of these properties form the basis of telomerase recognition.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of prior work.

claim: It was unknown which of the properties (parallel-stranded or intermolecular) form the basis of telomerase recognition.
source: Furthermore, since all previously-tested substrates were both parallel-stranded and intermolecular, it was unknown which of these properties form the basis of telomerase recognition.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the current study addresses.

claim: Wild-type human telomerase can unfold both intra- and intermolecular parallel G4 completely in the presence of dNTPs.
source: We provide direct evidence that wild-type human telomerase can unfold both intra- and intermolecular parallel G4 completely in the presence of dNTPs, using a 3-step mechanism.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Telomerase binds the G4, partially changing its conformation in a process that involves binding of the hTR template sequence.
source: First, telomerase binds the G4, partially changing its conformation in a process that involves binding of the hTR template sequence.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data and experiments with RNA oligonucleotides.

claim: Telomerase adds individual nucleotides to the 3' end of the partially unfolded parallel G4.
source: Second, telomerase adds individual nucleotides to the 3' end of the partially unfolded parallel G4.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with subsets of dNTPs.

claim: The translocation of telomerase results in complete disruption of the G4 structure.
source: Lastly, the translocation of telomerase results in complete disruption of the G4 structure.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data showing a second FRET drop after nucleotide addition reaches the template boundary.

claim: Stabilization of parallel intermolecular G4 using different G4 ligands did not inhibit telomerase unfolding and extension of this substrate.
source: Unexpectedly, stabilization of parallel intermolecular G4 using different G4 ligands did not inhibit telomerase unfolding and extension of this substrate.
evidence: This is supported by experiments with NMM, SST16, and PhenDC3 on [7GGT]4.

claim: Small molecule-mediated inhibition of telomerase extension of telomeric G4 is topology-dependent.
source: Overall, we provide a mechanistic explanation of conformation-specific telomerase extension of telomeric G4 at single-molecule resolution and demonstrate that small molecule-mediated inhibition of telomerase extension of telomeric G4 is topology-dependent.
evidence: This is supported by comparing the effects of ligands on intramolecular vs. intermolecular G4.

claim: Parallel, intermolecular G4 are substrates for telomerase.
source: Parallel, intermolecular G4 are substrates for telomerase, whereas intramolecular antiparallel or hybrid conformations are not (Hwang et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2017; Moye et al., 2015; Oganesian et al., 2006; Zahler et al., 1991; Zaug et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Intramolecular antiparallel or hybrid conformations are not substrates for telomerase.
source: Parallel, intermolecular G4 are substrates for telomerase, whereas intramolecular antiparallel or hybrid conformations are not (Hwang et al., 2014; Lee et al., 2017; Moye et al., 2015; Oganesian et al., 2006; Zahler et al., 1991; Zaug et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A 4-repeat human telomeric oligonucleotide does not readily fold into stable parallel intramolecular G4 at the concentrations used in in vitro assays.
source: Determining whether it is the parallel or intermolecular nature of G4 structures that allows their recognition by telomerase has been difficult, since a 4-repeat human telomeric oligonucleotide does not readily fold into stable parallel intramolecular G4 at the concentrations used in in vitro assays, and instead exists as a mixture of topologies under most conditions (Dai et al., 2007; Long and Stone, 2013; Palacký et al., 2013; Petraccone et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A 4-repeat human telomeric oligonucleotide exists as a mixture of topologies under most conditions.
source: Determining whether it is the parallel or intermolecular nature of G4 structures that allows their recognition by telomerase has been difficult, since a 4-repeat human telomeric oligonucleotide does not readily fold into stable parallel intramolecular G4 at the concentrations used in in vitro assays, and instead exists as a mixture of topologies under most conditions (Dai et al., 2007; Long and Stone, 2013; Palacký et al., 2013; Petraccone et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: 2'-fluoro-arabinoguanosine (2'F-araG) induces parallel propeller-type G4 conformations.
source: For this reason, we made use of the modified nucleotide 2'-fluoro-arabinoguanosine (2'F-araG), which induces parallel propeller-type G4 conformations (Peng and Damha, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Substitution of six guanosines in the telomeric sequence AGGG(TTAGGG)3 with 2'F-araG leads to a 15°C increase in Tm of the resulting intramolecular G4.
source: We have previously demonstrated that substitution of six guanosines in the telomeric sequence AGGG(TTAGGG)3 with 2'F-araG leads to a 15°C increase in Tm of the resulting intramolecular G4, and a shift from the usual antiparallel or hybrid topology of this sequence in potassium solution (Lim et al., 2009; Renciuk et al., 2009) to a parallel conformation (Figure 1A; Abou Assi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work from the authors.

claim: Substitution of six guanosines in the telomeric sequence AGGG(TTAGGG)3 with 2'F-araG leads to a shift from the usual antiparallel or hybrid topology to a parallel conformation.
source: We have previously demonstrated that substitution of six guanosines in the telomeric sequence AGGG(TTAGGG)3 with 2'F-araG leads to a 15°C increase in Tm of the resulting intramolecular G4, and a shift from the usual antiparallel or hybrid topology of this sequence in potassium solution (Lim et al., 2009; Renciuk et al., 2009) to a parallel conformation (Figure 1A; Abou Assi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work from the authors.

claim: G4 formed from the unmodified sequence (22G0) in KCl is a poor telomerase substrate, leading to the previously-observed stuttering pattern.
source: Here, we demonstrate that G4 formed from the unmodified sequence (22G0) in KCl is a poor telomerase substrate, leading to the previously-observed stuttering pattern (Zaug et al., 2005) in a direct telomerase extension assay involving incorporation of radiolabeled α32P-dGTP (Figure 1B, lane 3).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and a citation to prior literature.

claim: Substitution with 2'F-araG (22G3) restored the expected 6-nt repeat pattern of telomerase extension.
source: Substitution with 2'F-araG (22G3; see Supplementary file 1 for sequence) restored the expected 6-nt repeat pattern of telomerase extension (Figure 1B, lane 2), despite the increase in thermal stability of this G4.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Telomerase is able to extend parallel G4 structures, whether they are inter- or intramolecular.
source: Thus, telomerase is able to extend parallel G4 structures, whether they are inter- or intramolecular.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing 22G3 and [7GGT]4.

claim: Assembled F-22G3 was efficiently extended by telomerase.
source: Assembled F-22G3 was efficiently extended by telomerase, and was possibly an even better substrate than 22G3, with the expected 6-nt repeat pattern (Figure 1B, lane 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: F-22G3 was possibly an even better substrate than 22G3.
source: Assembled F-22G3 was efficiently extended by telomerase, and was possibly an even better substrate than 22G3, with the expected 6-nt repeat pattern (Figure 1B, lane 1).
evidence: This is a tentative inference based on experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Individual F-22G3 molecules all displayed a constant FRET ratio of ~0.5 over time.
source: Individual F-22G3 molecules all displayed a constant FRET ratio of ~0.5 over time, indicating that they did not undergo any detectable conformational changes in the experimental time window.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data presented in the manuscript.

claim: F-22G3 molecules did not undergo any detectable conformational changes in the experimental time window.
source: Individual F-22G3 molecules all displayed a constant FRET ratio of ~0.5 over time, indicating that they did not undergo any detectable conformational changes in the experimental time window.
evidence: This is an inference based on the constant FRET ratio observed in smFRET experiments.

claim: The calculated FRET efficiency for a distance of 51 Å between AF555 and AF647 is 0.44.
source: Given a Förster radius between AF555 and AF647 of 51 Å, the calculated FRET efficiency for this distance is 0.44, which is close to our experimental FRET value of 0.5.
evidence: This is a calculation based on known properties of the FRET dye pair.

claim: The experimental FRET value of F-22G3 is 0.5.
source: Given a Förster radius between AF555 and AF647 of 51 Å, the calculated FRET efficiency for this distance is 0.44, which is close to our experimental FRET value of 0.5.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data presented in the manuscript.

claim: In a majority of F-22G3 molecules, the FRET signal decreased from ~0.5 to ~0.14 and remained at the low FRET state during the entire observation window when KCl-containing buffer was substituted for a LiCl solution.
source: To confirm that this FRET value represents a G4 structure, we substituted the KCl-containing buffer for a LiCl solution, since Li+ does not support G4 formation; in a majority of molecules, the FRET signal decreased from ~0.5 to~0.14 and remained at the low FRET state during the entire observation window (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Li+ does not support G4 formation.
source: To confirm that this FRET value represents a G4 structure, we substituted the KCl-containing buffer for a LiCl solution, since Li+ does not support G4 formation; in a majority of molecules, the FRET signal decreased from ~0.5 to~0.14 and remained at the low FRET state during the entire observation window (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is established knowledge about G-quadruplex formation.

claim: The mean FRET value of F-22G3 in KCl is 0.53 ± 0.05.
source: The heat map showed that the mean FRET value (0.53 ± 0.05) remained unchanged over time; an alternative histogram representation of the same data grouped into 15 s bins confirms this conclusion (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The F-22G3 G-quadruplex is stable over time.
source: These data demonstrate that the F-22G3 G-quadruplex is stable over time.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the constant FRET value observed over time.

claim: Approximately 65% of F-22G3 molecules showed an abrupt drop in FRET value, from 0.53 ± 0.05 to 0.3 ± 0.1, during the 160 s after telomerase was injected.
source: Approximately 65% of F-22G3 molecules showed an abrupt drop in FRET value, from 0.53 ± 0.05 to 0.3 ± 0.1, during the 160 s after telomerase was injected into the microscopic channel containing immobilized F-22G3 (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: The remaining 35% of F-22G3 molecules did not show any change in FRET signal over the observed time in the presence of telomerase.
source: The remaining 35% of molecules did not show any change in FRET signal over the observed time; it is possible that the binding reaction had not proceeded to completion within this time period, or that a subpopulation of enzyme or DNA molecules are incompetent for binding.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data and includes speculation about the reasons.

claim: Telomerase binding to F-22G3 partially opens the structure, which then remains stable in its new conformation.
source: We interpret this to represent telomerase binding to F-22G3 and partially opening the structure, which then remained stable in its new conformation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the smFRET data showing a single FRET drop in the presence of telomerase.

claim: In the presence of telomerase, the TDP showed a single cluster of transitions at initial FRET ~ 0.5 and final FRET ~ 0.3.
source: In the presence of telomerase, the TDP showed a single cluster of transitions at initial FRET ~ 0.5 and final FRET ~ 0.3, consistent with the shift in mean FRET in the heat map.
evidence: This is supported by TDP analysis shown in Figure 2F.

claim: In the presence of both telomerase and dNTPs, ~65% of F-22G3 molecules showed a two-step drop in FRET values, from 0.53 ± 0.05 to 0.3 ± 0.1, and then to 0.15 ± 0.05.
source: Under these conditions,~65% of molecules showed a two-step drop in FRET values, from 0.53 ± 0.05 to 0.3 ± 0.1, and then to 0.15 ± 0.05 (Figure 2C and G–I, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 2C, G-I, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: The FRET decrease from high to low FRET states in the presence of telomerase and dNTPs was irreversible.
source: The FRET decrease from high to low FRET states in these events was irreversible, supported by the presence of two off-diagonal clusters in the TDP (Figure 2I), suggesting a continuous irreversible unfolding of G4 structure.
evidence: This is supported by TDP analysis shown in Figure 2I.

claim: Telomerase disrupts F-22G3 structure completely in the presence of dNTPs.
source: These data suggest that telomerase disrupts F-22G3 structure completely in the presence of dNTPs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the two-step FRET drop observed in smFRET experiments.

claim: F-22G3 molecules exhibited telomerase-mediated unfolding with a rate constant of kunfolding = 0.120 ± 0.013 s−1.
source: F-22G3 molecules exhibited telomerase-mediated unfolding with a rate constant of kunfolding = 0.120 ± 0.013 s−1 (mean ± SEM).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of dwell time distributions from smFRET data.

claim: The unfolding rate of F-22G3 by telomerase is comparable with the rate of unfolding of parallel G4 by Pif1 helicase (0.11 s−1).
source: This unfolding rate is comparable with the rate of unfolding of parallel G4 by Pif1 helicase (0.11 s−1) (Byrd and Raney, 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison with a rate from prior literature.

claim: The number of rate-limiting steps in F-22G3 unfolding by telomerase is 2.8.
source: Gamma distributions also provide information about the number of rate-limiting steps within a complex kinetic process (Floyd et al., 2010); in this case, the number of steps (N) is 2.8 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), suggesting that unfolding is a complex process involving at least 2–3 kinetic steps.
evidence: This is supported by gamma distribution analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Unfolding of F-22G3 by telomerase is a complex process involving at least 2–3 kinetic steps.
source: Gamma distributions also provide information about the number of rate-limiting steps within a complex kinetic process (Floyd et al., 2010); in this case, the number of steps (N) is 2.8 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), suggesting that unfolding is a complex process involving at least 2–3 kinetic steps.
evidence: This is an inference based on gamma distribution analysis.

claim: A tetrameric, parallel G4 formed from four copies of the 7-mer telomeric sequence TTAGGGT in K+ is highly stable.
source: We have previously demonstrated that a tetrameric, parallel G4 (Gavathiotis and Searle, 2003) formed from four copies of the 7-mer telomeric sequence TTAGGGT in K+ is highly stable but can be extended by human telomerase (Moye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: A tetrameric, parallel G4 formed from four copies of the 7-mer telomeric sequence TTAGGGT can be extended by human telomerase.
source: We have previously demonstrated that a tetrameric, parallel G4 (Gavathiotis and Searle, 2003) formed from four copies of the 7-mer telomeric sequence TTAGGGT in K+ is highly stable but can be extended by human telomerase (Moye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work from the authors.

claim: The sequence TTAGGGT is too short to form intramolecular G4 structures, and can only exist as a parallel tetramer.
source: This sequence provides the advantage that the conformation of its G4 topology is unambiguous; the sequence is too short to form intramolecular G4 structures, and can only exist as a parallel tetramer.
evidence: This is an inference based on the length and sequence of the oligonucleotide.

claim: Human telomerase can extend the FRET-modified G4 construct (F-[7GGT]4) as efficiently as the unmodified [7GGT]4.
source: Direct telomerase activity assays demonstrated that human telomerase can extend the FRET-modified G4 construct (which we refer to as F-[7GGT]4) as efficiently as the unmodified [7GGT]4 (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Most F-[7GGT]4 molecules exhibit a steady FRET signal at a ratio of ~0.6.
source: smFRET experiments showed that most F-[7GGT]4 molecules exhibit a steady FRET signal at a ratio of ~0.6, and the FRET signal did not change over time (Figure 4A and B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating formation of a stable parallel intermolecular G4.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 4A, B, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The FRET signal of F-[7GGT]4 did not change over time.
source: smFRET experiments showed that most F-[7GGT]4 molecules exhibit a steady FRET signal at a ratio of ~0.6, and the FRET signal did not change over time (Figure 4A and B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating formation of a stable parallel intermolecular G4.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 4A, B, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: F-[7GGT]4 forms a stable parallel intermolecular G4.
source: smFRET experiments showed that most F-[7GGT]4 molecules exhibit a steady FRET signal at a ratio of ~0.6, and the FRET signal did not change over time (Figure 4A and B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), indicating formation of a stable parallel intermolecular G4.
evidence: This is an inference based on the constant FRET signal observed in smFRET experiments.

claim: Substitution of the K+-containing buffer for one containing Li+ resulted in a drop to a stable FRET value of ~0.2 for F-[7GGT]4, followed by complete loss of the signal from both dyes.
source: Substitution of the K+-containing buffer for one containing Li+ resulted in a drop to a stable FRET value of ~0.2, followed by complete loss of the signal from both dyes, likely representing G4 unwinding followed by loss of the non-biotinylated dye-bearing strands (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Telomerase alone was sufficient for partial unwinding of parallel F-[7GGT]4.
source: Telomerase alone was sufficient for partial unwinding of parallel F-[7GGT]4, as demonstrated by a drop in FRET state from ~0.6 to~0.4 with time (Figure 4D–F, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 4D-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: About 60% of F-[7GGT]4 molecules showed a one-step drop in FRET signal upon injection of telomerase.
source: About 60% of molecules showed this one-step drop in FRET signal upon injection of telomerase (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Telomerase results in a partial separation of the FRET dyes upon binding to one strand of the tetrameric G4.
source: In the case of the 60% of molecules that do show a drop in FRET signal, we interpret this to demonstrate that telomerase results in a partial separation of the FRET dyes upon binding to one strand of the tetrameric G4.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the smFRET data showing a single FRET drop in the presence of telomerase.

claim: In the presence of telomerase and dNTPs, most F-[7GGT]4 molecules experienced a two-step drop in FRET, from 0.57 ± 0.05 to 0.36 ± 0.04, and then to 0.19 ± 0.05.
source: In the presence of telomerase and dNTPs, most F-[7GGT]4 molecules experienced a two-step drop in FRET, from 0.57 ± 0.05 to 0.36 ± 0.04, and then to 0.19 ± 0.05 (Figure 4C and G–I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D); this transition did not occur in the presence of dNTPs alone (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 4C, G-I, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: The two-step FRET drop in F-[7GGT]4 did not occur in the presence of dNTPs alone.
source: In the presence of telomerase and dNTPs, most F-[7GGT]4 molecules experienced a two-step drop in FRET, from 0.57 ± 0.05 to 0.36 ± 0.04, and then to 0.19 ± 0.05 (Figure 4C and G–I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and D); this transition did not occur in the presence of dNTPs alone (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by control experiments shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Telomerase unfolds parallel intermolecular G4 irreversibly.
source: The two FRET transition clusters observed by TDP analysis (Figure 4I) suggest that telomerase unfolds parallel intermolecular G4 irreversibly.
evidence: This is an inference based on TDP analysis shown in Figure 4I.

claim: The low FRET state of F-[7GGT]4 (~0.2) is consistent with the low FRET state observed during Li+-mediated G4 unfolding.
source: The low FRET state of ~0.2 is consistent with the low FRET state observed during Li+-mediated G4 unfolding (Figure 4—figure supplement 2); surprisingly, however, we did not observe complete loss of FRET signal (i.e. disappearance of both dyes simultaneously), as we had seen in the presence of Li+.
evidence: This is a comparison between two experimental conditions.

claim: Complete loss of FRET signal was not observed for F-[7GGT]4 in the presence of telomerase and dNTPs, unlike in the presence of Li+.
source: The low FRET state of ~0.2 is consistent with the low FRET state observed during Li+-mediated G4 unfolding (Figure 4—figure supplement 2); surprisingly, however, we did not observe complete loss of FRET signal (i.e. disappearance of both dyes simultaneously), as we had seen in the presence of Li+.
evidence: This is an observation from smFRET experiments.

claim: While telomerase extension results in G4 disruption, the presence of the enzyme keeps the four strands in proximity of each other.
source: This suggests that while telomerase extension results in G4 disruption, the presence of the enzyme keeps the four strands in proximity of each other, rather than allowing them to completely diffuse apart.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observation that FRET signal is maintained at ~0.2 rather than being completely lost.

claim: The rate of unfolding of F-[7GGT]4 by telomerase in the presence of dNTPs is kunfolding = 0.073 ± 0.013 s−1.
source: The rate of unfolding of F-[7GGT]4 by telomerase in the presence of dNTPs was measured by plotting the dwell times of the intermediate transition states (FRET value of 0.4) and fitting them to a gamma distribution that yielded kunfolding = 0.073 ± 0.013 s−1 (mean ± SEM; Figure 4—figure supplement 4A), with N = 2.3 ± 0.1.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of dwell time distributions from smFRET data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The rate of unfolding of [7GGT]4 by telomerase in the presence of dNTPs is comparable to that of F-22G3.
source: Thus, the rate of unfolding of [7GGT]4 by telomerase in the presence of dNTPs is comparable to that of F-22G3.
evidence: This is a comparison between the unfolding rates of the two G4 structures.

claim: The gamma distribution suggested that 2–3 rate-limiting steps contribute to the unfolding rate of F-[7GGT]4.
source: The gamma distribution also suggested that 2–3 rate-limiting steps contribute to this rate.
evidence: This is an inference based on gamma distribution analysis.

claim: At a 100-fold lower concentration of dGTP, ~40% of F-[7GGT]4 traces showed a plateau at FRET ~ 0.4 followed by a gradual transition to ~0.2.
source: To explore this, we carried out smFRET analyses of [7GGT]4 in the presence of a 100-fold lower concentration of dGTP; this resulted in ~40% of traces that showed a plateau at FRET ~ 0.4 followed by a gradual transition to ~0.2 (example in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: At low dGTP concentration, the kunfolding of F-[7GGT]4 is 0.040 ± 0.006 s−1, which is ~1.8 fold slower than the rate at a high dGTP concentration.
source: Quantitation of the dwell times at FRET 0.4 showed a kunfolding of 0.040 ± 0.006 s−1 (mean ± SEM; Figure 4—figure supplement 4C), which is ~1.8 fold slower than the rate at a high dGTP concentration, and N = 2.10 ± 0.03.
evidence: This is supported by analysis of dwell time distributions from smFRET data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4C.

claim: The rate of the gradual transition from FRET 0.4 to 0.2 at low dGTP concentration is 0.44 ± 0.14 s−1, with 3–4 rate-limiting steps.
source: Approximation of the times taken for the gradual transition to FRET 0.2 (that we refer to as τunfolding-2) yielded a rate of 0.44 ± 0.14 s−1, with 3–4 rate-limiting steps revealed by the gamma distribution (Figure 4—figure supplement 4D).
evidence: This is supported by analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4D.

claim: The process of G4 unfolding by telomerase is complex and involves at least five independent steps.
source: Together, these data suggest that the process of G4 unfolding by telomerase is complex and involves at least five independent steps, whose rates are influenced by dNTP concentration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the gamma distribution analyses at different dGTP concentrations.

claim: The rates of G4 unfolding steps are influenced by dNTP concentration.
source: Together, these data suggest that the process of G4 unfolding by telomerase is complex and involves at least five independent steps, whose rates are influenced by dNTP concentration.
evidence: This is supported by the observation that unfolding rates differ at high and low dGTP concentrations.

claim: Mutation of any one of three conserved aspartate residues in the reverse transcriptase domain of TERT results in loss of telomerase catalytic activity but retention of its ability to bind to a DNA primer.
source: Synthesis activity requires three conserved aspartate residues in the reverse transcriptase domain of the TERT protein (Counter et al., 1997; Harrington et al., 1997; Lingner et al., 1997; Weinrich et al., 1997). Mutation of any one of these aspartates results in loss of telomerase catalytic activity but retention of its ability to bind to a DNA primer (Wyatt et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: D712A telomerase lost all primer extension activity.
source: We introduced an aspartate-to-alanine mutation at hTERT amino acid 712 and confirmed that this mutant telomerase (D712A) lost all primer extension activity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: smFRET experiments with F-[7GGT]4 demonstrated an initial drop in FRET after addition of D712A telomerase, but no further drop in FRET was observed upon addition of dNTPs.
source: smFRET experiments with F-[7GGT]4 demonstrated an initial drop in FRET after addition of D712A telomerase, but no further drop in FRET was observed upon addition of dNTPs (Figure 5A–E).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 5A-E.

claim: Binding of telomerase to F-[7GGT]4, resulting in partial G4 unwinding, is independent of telomerase catalytic activity.
source: This result suggests that binding of telomerase to F-[7GGT]4, resulting in partial G4 unwinding, is independent of telomerase catalytic activity, but full unwinding of the G4 requires its extension by telomerase.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that D712A telomerase causes a single FRET drop but not a second drop.

claim: Full unwinding of the G4 requires its extension by telomerase.
source: This result suggests that binding of telomerase to F-[7GGT]4, resulting in partial G4 unwinding, is independent of telomerase catalytic activity, but full unwinding of the G4 requires its extension by telomerase.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that D712A telomerase causes a single FRET drop but not a second drop.

claim: The RNA template of telomerase plays an important role in recognizing and binding the telomeric end by canonical base pairing.
source: It is known that the RNA template of telomerase plays an important role in recognizing and binding the telomeric end by canonical base paring.
evidence: This is established knowledge about telomerase function.

claim: [7GGT]4 is extended by the nucleotides that would be predicted from canonical base-pairing with the RNA template.
source: We have previously demonstrated that [7GGT]4 is extended by the nucleotides that would be predicted from canonical base-pairing with the RNA template (Moye et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work from the authors.

claim: The RNA template binds to the G4, facilitating the opening of the structure.
source: Therefore, we hypothesized that the RNA template binds to the G4, facilitating the opening of the structure.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that is tested in the subsequent experiments.

claim: At a high concentration of RNA.10C (500 μM), a majority of F-[7GGT]4 molecules executed a single-step drop in FRET from 0.57 to 0.36.
source: At a high concentration of RNA.10C (500 μM), a majority of F-[7GGT]4 molecules executed a single-step drop in FRET from 0.57 to 0.36 (Figure 5F,G and J); thus, a short oligonucleotide resembling the telomerase template induces G4 unfolding in a similar manner to the whole telomerase enzyme.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 5F, G, and J.

claim: A short oligonucleotide resembling the telomerase template induces G4 unfolding in a similar manner to the whole telomerase enzyme.
source: At a high concentration of RNA.10C (500 μM), a majority of F-[7GGT]4 molecules executed a single-step drop in FRET from 0.57 to 0.36 (Figure 5F,G and J); thus, a short oligonucleotide resembling the telomerase template induces G4 unfolding in a similar manner to the whole telomerase enzyme.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the smFRET data with RNA.10C.

claim: The fraction of the G4 population that showed a drop in FRET signal was dependent on the concentration of RNA.10C.
source: The fraction of the G4 population that showed a drop in FRET signal was dependent on the concentration of RNA.10C (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B), and at both concentrations ~ 20% of the molecules showed dynamic behaviour during the observation window, transiently returning to the high FRET state (examples in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C and D), which was not observed in experiments with the whole telomerase enzyme.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: At both concentrations of RNA.10C, ~ 20% of the molecules showed dynamic behaviour during the observation window, transiently returning to the high FRET state.
source: The fraction of the G4 population that showed a drop in FRET signal was dependent on the concentration of RNA.10C (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B), and at both concentrations ~ 20% of the molecules showed dynamic behaviour during the observation window, transiently returning to the high FRET state (examples in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C and D), which was not observed in experiments with the whole telomerase enzyme.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: The affinity of the RNA oligonucleotide for the G4 is lower than that of telomerase.
source: This indicates that the affinity of the RNA oligonucleotide for the G4 is lower than that of telomerase, which is not unexpected given the multiple protein-DNA contacts that can occur in the presence of hTERT.
evidence: This is an inference based on the dynamic behavior observed with RNA.10C but not with telomerase.

claim: The presence of 500 µM of a 10-nt DNA oligonucleotide of identical sequence (DNA.10C) did not stimulate any change in the FRET signal of F-[7GGT]4 over the same time period.
source: Nevertheless, the effect of an oligonucleotide on G4 structure was very specific to RNA; the presence of 500 µM of a 10-nt DNA oligonucleotide of identical sequence (DNA.10C) did not stimulate any change in the FRET signal of F-[7GGT]4 over the same time period (Figure 5H–J).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 5H-J.

claim: The hTR template is specifically involved in binding to the G4, leading to partial opening of the structure.
source: These data suggest that the hTR template is specifically involved in binding to the G4, leading to partial opening of the structure.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of RNA.10C and DNA.10C effects.

claim: The second step of telomerase-mediated unfolding of G4 DNA requires telomerase catalytic activity.
source: The second step of telomerase-mediated unfolding of G4 DNA requires telomerase catalytic activity (Figure 5C–E).
evidence: This is supported by experiments with D712A telomerase shown in Figure 5C-E.

claim: In the presence of only ddTTP, F-22G3 exhibited a FRET drop from ~0.5 to ~0.3 and remained in the ~0.3 FRET state over the remainder of the observation time window.
source: Under these conditions, F-22G3 exhibited a FRET drop from ~0.5 to~0.3 and remained in the ~0.3 FRET state over the remainder of the observation time window (Figure 6B–D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 6B-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: A similar change in FRET from ~0.5 to ~0.3 was observed when the only nucleotides in the reaction were dTTP and ddATP.
source: A similar change in FRET from ~0.5 to~0.3 was observed when the only nucleotides in the reaction were dTTP and ddATP (Figure 6F–H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 6F-H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the presence of dTTP, dATP and ddGTP, a second step-wise drop in FRET was exhibited by F-22G3, from ~0.3 to ~0.15.
source: However, in the presence of dTTP, dATP and ddGTP, a second step-wise drop in FRET was exhibited by F-22G3, from ~0.3 to~0.15 (Figure 6J–L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 6J-L and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Complete G4 unfolding occurs after the addition of three nucleotides complementary to the template.
source: These data demonstrate that complete G4 unfolding occurs after the addition of three nucleotides complementary to the template; at this point, the template boundary is reached and translocation of the DNA to the 3' region of the template is likely to occur (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments with subsets of dNTPs.

claim: At the point when three nucleotides have been added, the template boundary is reached and translocation of the DNA to the 3' region of the template is likely to occur.
source: These data demonstrate that complete G4 unfolding occurs after the addition of three nucleotides complementary to the template; at this point, the template boundary is reached and translocation of the DNA to the 3' region of the template is likely to occur (Figure 6I).
evidence: This is an inference based on the known mechanism of telomerase and the observation of complete unfolding after three nucleotide additions.

claim: The FRET signal of F-[7GGT]4 dropped in a single step, from ~0.6 to ~0.4, in the presence of telomerase and either ddTTP alone or dTTP and ddATP.
source: The FRET signal dropped in a single step, from ~0.6 to~0.4, in the presence of telomerase and either ddTTP alone or dTTP and ddATP.
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: In the presence of telomerase and dTTP, dATP and ddGTP, F-[7GGT]4 showed a two-step decrease, from a high FRET state (~0.6) to ~0.4 and then to the lowest FRET state (~0.2).
source: However, in the presence of telomerase and dTTP, dATP and ddGTP, a two-step decrease was observed, from a high FRET state (~0.6) to ~0.4 and then to the lowest FRET state (~0.2) (Figure 6—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2 and 3.

claim: Telomerase binds and unfolds parallel G4 using a similar mechanism, whether the strand topology is intramolecular or intermolecular.
source: Overall, these data demonstrate that telomerase binds and unfolds parallel G4 using a similar mechanism, whether the strand topology is intramolecular or intermolecular.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the mechanisms observed for F-22G3 and F-[7GGT]4.

claim: Antiparallel or hybrid telomeric G4 are not efficiently used as substrates by telomerase.
source: Antiparallel or hybrid telomeric G4 are not efficiently used as substrates by telomerase, and their stabilization with small molecule G4-binding ligands can further decrease the ability of telomerase to extend them (De Cian et al., 2007a; Zahler et al., 1991; Zaug et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Stabilization of antiparallel or hybrid telomeric G4 with small molecule G4-binding ligands can further decrease the ability of telomerase to extend them.
source: Antiparallel or hybrid telomeric G4 are not efficiently used as substrates by telomerase, and their stabilization with small molecule G4-binding ligands can further decrease the ability of telomerase to extend them (De Cian et al., 2007a; Zahler et al., 1991; Zaug et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: None of the ligands (NMM, SST16, PhenDC3) substantially changed the overall parallel G4 conformation of F-22G3.
source: CD spectroscopy confirmed that none of the ligands substantially changed the overall parallel G4 conformation of F-22G3 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–C), and melting assays showed dramatic thermal stabilization of this G4 upon binding by all three ligands (ΔTm of >25°C (NMM), +11°C (SST16) and >25°C (PhenDC3), under the conditions detailed in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D–F).
evidence: This is supported by CD spectroscopy data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Melting assays showed dramatic thermal stabilization of F-22G3 upon binding by all three ligands (ΔTm of >25°C (NMM), +11°C (SST16) and >25°C (PhenDC3)).
source: CD spectroscopy confirmed that none of the ligands substantially changed the overall parallel G4 conformation of F-22G3 (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A–C), and melting assays showed dramatic thermal stabilization of this G4 upon binding by all three ligands (ΔTm of >25°C (NMM), +11°C (SST16) and >25°C (PhenDC3), under the conditions detailed in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D–F).
evidence: This is supported by melting assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2D-F.

claim: The ligands did not change the steady smFRET signal of F-22G3 in the absence of telomerase.
source: The ligands did not change the steady smFRET signal of F-22G3 in the absence of telomerase (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: In the presence of telomerase, dNTPs and each of the three ligands, the number of F-22G3 molecules experiencing a two-step FRET decrease was reduced by about 2-fold.
source: In the presence of telomerase, dNTPs and each of the three ligands, the number of molecules experiencing a two-step FRET decrease was reduced by about 2-fold, and the number of molecules with no FRET changes doubled (Figure 7A–J).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 7A-J.

claim: In the presence of telomerase, dNTPs and each of the three ligands, the number of F-22G3 molecules with no FRET changes doubled.
source: In the presence of telomerase, dNTPs and each of the three ligands, the number of molecules experiencing a two-step FRET decrease was reduced by about 2-fold, and the number of molecules with no FRET changes doubled (Figure 7A–J).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 7A-J.

claim: The ligands reduce binding of telomerase to F-22G3, preventing induction of the first step of FRET decrease.
source: This suggests that the ligands reduce binding of telomerase to this G4, preventing induction of the first step of FRET decrease.
evidence: This is an inference based on the increased number of molecules with no FRET changes in the presence of ligands.

claim: 25–30% of F-22G3 molecules showed the same FRET decrease from ~0.5 to ~0.3 and then to ~0.15 as in the absence of ligands.
source: Nevertheless, 25–30% of molecules showed the same FRET decrease from ~0.5 to~0.3 and then to ~0.15 as in the absence of ligands (Figure 7A–J).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 7A-J.

claim: The rates of telomerase-mediated unfolding of NMM-, SST16- and PhenDC3-stabilized F-22G3 were 0.071 ± 0.014 s−1 (N = 2.50 ± 0.04), 0.096 ± 0.01 s−1 (N = 2.6 ± 0.1), and 0.098 ± 0.015 s−1 (N = 2.60 ± 0.05), respectively.
source: The rates of telomerase-mediated unfolding of NMM-, SST16- and PhenDC3-stabilized F-22G3 were 0.071 ± 0.014 s−1 (N = 2.50 ± 0.04), 0.096 ± 0.01 s−1 (N = 2.6 ± 0.1), and 0.098 ± 0.015 s−1 (N = 2.60 ± 0.05), respectively (mean ± SEM; Figure 7K, Figure 7—figure supplement 4); in the case of NMM, this was significantly slower (p=0.0118; Student's t-test) than in the absence of ligands (0.12 ± 0.013 s−1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of dwell time distributions from smFRET data shown in Figure 7K and Figure 7—figure supplement 4.

claim: In the case of NMM, the unfolding rate was significantly slower (p=0.0118) than in the absence of ligands (0.12 ± 0.013 s−1).
source: The rates of telomerase-mediated unfolding of NMM-, SST16- and PhenDC3-stabilized F-22G3 were 0.071 ± 0.014 s−1 (N = 2.50 ± 0.04), 0.096 ± 0.01 s−1 (N = 2.6 ± 0.1), and 0.098 ± 0.015 s−1 (N = 2.60 ± 0.05), respectively (mean ± SEM; Figure 7K, Figure 7—figure supplement 4); in the case of NMM, this was significantly slower (p=0.0118; Student's t-test) than in the absence of ligands (0.12 ± 0.013 s−1).
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the unfolding rates.

claim: The reduced rate of G4 unfolding in the presence of NMM provides evidence that most or all of these molecules were bound by ligands.
source: At least in the case of NMM, the reduced rate of G4 unfolding provides evidence that most or all of these molecules were bound by ligands, but that ligand presence slowed the rate of their unfolding by telomerase.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced unfolding rate in the presence of NMM.

claim: Ligand presence slowed the rate of F-22G3 unfolding by telomerase.
source: At least in the case of NMM, the reduced rate of G4 unfolding provides evidence that most or all of these molecules were bound by ligands, but that ligand presence slowed the rate of their unfolding by telomerase.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced unfolding rate in the presence of NMM.

claim: All three ligands partially inhibited telomerase extension of F-22G3 when incubated at the same concentrations in ensemble telomerase activity assays.
source: Consistent with these data, all three ligands partially inhibited telomerase extension of F-22G3 when incubated at the same concentrations in ensemble telomerase activity assays (Figure 7—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is supported by ensemble activity assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 5.

claim: PhenDC3 caused a substantial loss of activity on a linear DNA substrate.
source: PhenDC3 resulted in a more dramatic decrease in activity than in G4 unfolding measured by smFRET, but it also caused a substantial loss of activity on a linear DNA substrate, consistent with its previously-described effects on telomerase in a manner independent of G4 (De Cian et al., 2007a).
evidence: This is supported by ensemble activity assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 5.

claim: PhenDC3 has previously-described effects on telomerase in a manner independent of G4.
source: PhenDC3 resulted in a more dramatic decrease in activity than in G4 unfolding measured by smFRET, but it also caused a substantial loss of activity on a linear DNA substrate, consistent with its previously-described effects on telomerase in a manner independent of G4 (De Cian et al., 2007a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Telomerase unfolding and extension of an intramolecular parallel G4 are partially inhibited by ligand stabilization.
source: Together, these data suggest that telomerase unfolding and extension of an intramolecular parallel G4 are partially inhibited by ligand stabilization; nevertheless, telomerase is able to overcome this stabilization and unwind a substantial proportion (25–30%) of molecules (Figure 7J).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the smFRET and ensemble activity assay data with ligands.

claim: Telomerase is able to overcome ligand stabilization and unwind a substantial proportion (25–30%) of F-22G3 molecules.
source: Together, these data suggest that telomerase unfolding and extension of an intramolecular parallel G4 are partially inhibited by ligand stabilization; nevertheless, telomerase is able to overcome this stabilization and unwind a substantial proportion (25–30%) of molecules (Figure 7J).
evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 7J.

claim: None of the ligands (NMM, SST16, PhenDC3) substantially changed the parallel G4 conformation of [7GGT]4.
source: CD spectroscopy confirmed that none of the ligands substantially changed the parallel G4 conformation of [7GGT]4 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by CD spectroscopy data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Melting assays showed dramatic thermal stabilization of [7GGT]4 upon binding by all three ligands (ΔTm of +13°C (NMM), +21°C (SST16) and +26°C (PhenDC3)).
source: Melting assays showed dramatic thermal stabilization of [7GGT]4 upon binding by all three ligands (ΔTm of +13°C (NMM), +21°C (SST16) and +26°C (PhenDC3), under the conditions detailed in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: This is supported by melting assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1D-F.

claim: Stabilization of [7GGT]4 with ligands did not inhibit its extension by telomerase.
source: Telomerase activity assays were carried out at the same concentrations of [7GGT]4 and each ligand as used in CD analyses; surprisingly, stabilization of the G-quadruplex did not inhibit its extension by telomerase (Figure 8A–D).
evidence: This is supported by ensemble activity assay data shown in Figure 8A-D.

claim: PhenDC3 caused a decrease in enzyme processivity after the addition of 4 telomeric repeats to either a linear or a G4 substrate.
source: As previously described (De Cian et al., 2007a), PhenDC3 caused a decrease in enzyme processivity after the addition of 4 telomeric repeats to either a linear or a G4 substrate (Figure 8C), most likely resulting from stabilization of the G-quadruplexes that have been demonstrated to occur within telomerase product DNA (Jansson et al., 2019; Patrick et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by ensemble activity assay data shown in Figure 8C and citations to prior literature.

claim: The decrease in enzyme processivity caused by PhenDC3 most likely results from stabilization of the G-quadruplexes that occur within telomerase product DNA.
source: As previously described (De Cian et al., 2007a), PhenDC3 caused a decrease in enzyme processivity after the addition of 4 telomeric repeats to either a linear or a G4 substrate (Figure 8C), most likely resulting from stabilization of the G-quadruplexes that have been demonstrated to occur within telomerase product DNA (Jansson et al., 2019; Patrick et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on prior literature about G4 formation in telomerase products.

claim: Concentrations of PhenDC3 higher than 1 µM caused dramatic inhibition of activity.

evidence: This is supported by ensemble activity assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Substantial stabilization of a parallel intermolecular G4 by three different ligands did not inhibit the ability of telomerase to use the G4 as a substrate.

claim: Ligand-stabilized F-[7GGT]4 exhibited a constant FRET signal at 0.57.

claim: In the presence of telomerase, a single-step FRET decrease from 0.57 to 0.36 was observed in a majority of ligand-stabilized F-[7GGT]4 single-molecule traces.

claim: Ligand binding to F-[7GGT]4 did not prevent telomerase from inducing a conformational change in the G4.

evidence: This is supported by smFRET data shown in Figure 9A-J.

claim: The rates of telomerase-mediated unfolding of NMM-, SST16- and PhenDC3-stabilized F-[7GGT]4 were 0.090 ± 0.017 s−1 (N = 2.40 ± 0.04), 0.28 ± 0.07 s−1 (N = 3.7 ± 0.1), and 0.15 ± 0.05 s−1 (N = 2.9 ± 0.1), respectively.

evidence: This is supported by analysis of dwell time distributions from smFRET data shown in Figure 9K and Figure 9—figure supplement 3.

claim: In the presence of SST16, unfolding of F-[7GGT]4 occurred significantly faster (p=0.021) than in the absence of ligands (0.073 ± 0.013 s−1).

evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of the unfolding rates.

claim: Neither unwinding nor extension of parallel intermolecular G4 by telomerase were inhibited by ligand-mediated stabilization of the G4.

evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the smFRET and ensemble activity assay data with [7GGT]4 and ligands.

claim: Molecular dynamic simulations showed the 5' ends of the G4 DNA strands moving apart from one another after 100 ns.

evidence: This is supported by molecular dynamics simulation results shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Binding of the G4 to telomerase may result in an increase in distance between the dyes.

evidence: This is an inference based on molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: Telomerase has the ability to unwind parallel G4, without the assistance of interacting helicases.

claim: Telomerase partially unfolds parallel G4, independently of telomerase catalytic activity.

claim: Binding of telomerase RNA to the nucleotides at the 3' end of one DNA strand allows RNA-DNA hybridization to occur while resulting in a conformational perturbation of the 5' end of the G4.

evidence: This is an interpretation of the smFRET data, supported by molecular modeling shown in Figure 10B and C.

claim: It is the RNA component of telomerase, rather than the hTERT protein, that promotes the initial unwinding of parallel G4, followed by hybridization to the 3' end.
source: This observation suggests that it is the RNA component of telomerase, rather than the hTERT protein, that promotes the initial unwinding of parallel G4, followed by hybridization to the 3' end.

claim: A template-mimicking RNA was unable to form a DNA-RNA hybrid with an antiparallel G4 of similar stability to the parallel G4 used in the present study.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the effects of RNA on parallel vs. antiparallel G4.

claim: Telomerase extends the 3' end of parallel G4 while the G4 remains partially structured.

evidence: This is supported by experiments with subsets of dNTPs shown in Figure 6.

claim: ddGTP incorporation is compatible with subsequent DNA realignment and rehybridization with the upstream region of the template.
source: Although these experiments involved incorporation of a chain terminating ddGTP, it has been demonstrated by smFRET that ddGTP incorporation is compatible with subsequent DNA realignment and rehybridization with the upstream region of the template (Parks and Stone, 2014); it is therefore likely that conformational changes involved in the translocation process result in complete G4 unfolding, represented by a second step-wise drop in FRET signal.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Conformational changes involved in the translocation process result in complete G4 unfolding.
source: Although these experiments involved incorporation of a chain terminating ddGTP, it has been demonstrated by smFRET that ddGTP incorporation is compatible with subsequent DNA realignment and rehybridization with the upstream region of the template (Parks and Stone, 2014); it is therefore likely that conformational changes involved in the translocation process result in complete G4 unfolding, represented by a second step-wise drop in FRET signal.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of a second FRET drop after nucleotide addition reaches the template boundary.

claim: The G4 structure needs to pass through the telomerase DNA-binding cleft during the conformation changes required for telomerase translocation, and the resulting steric hindrance results in complete dissociation of the parallel telomeric G4.
source: One possible explanation for this observation is that the G4 structure needs to pass through the telomerase DNA-binding cleft during the conformation changes required for telomerase translocation, and the resulting steric hindrance results in complete dissociation of the parallel telomeric G4.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed complete G4 unfolding.

claim: Telomerase is able to dislodge ligands from the tetramolecular G4 structure while unfolding it.
source: This observation suggests that, like other proteins such as RHAU helicase (Gueddouda et al., 2017; Tippana et al., 2016), telomerase is able to dislodge ligands from the tetramolecular G4 structure while unfolding it.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that telomerase can unfold ligand-stabilized [7GGT]4.

claim: This displacement mechanism would have implications for interpreting the biological effects of G4-stabilizing ligands in cell-based studies.
source: This displacement activity is structure dependent, since telomerase is less able to dislodge ligands from a parallel intramolecular G4, possibly due to the presence of DNA loops. Such a displacement mechanism would have implications for interpreting the biological effects of G4-stabilizing ligands in cell-based studies, since any effects on telomerase action and telomere length will depend on the conformational specificity of the ligand.
evidence: This is a speculation about the implications of the findings.
